brief.ticker: Private ($8.6B post-money; $1.5B Series D, Feb 2026, extended Apr 2026)
brief.deck: Wayve, the London embodied-AI company whose AI Driver Nissan will ship in next-generation ProPILOT from fiscal 2027, extended its Series D on 15 April 2026 with $60M from AMD, Arm and Qualcomm Ventures, on top of the $1.2B round at an $8.6B valuation closed in February with Nissan aboard.
brief.the_case_p1: On 15 April Wayve announced a $60M Series D extension from AMD, Arm and Qualcomm Ventures, adding the three chipmakers to a round that closed on 24 February at $1.2B and an $8.6B post-money valuation, led by Eclipse, Balderton and SoftBank Vision Fund 2 with Microsoft, Nvidia and Uber, $1.5B in total with Uber's milestone capital. Nissan, Mercedes-Benz and Stellantis invested as automakers. Nissan signed definitive agreements in December 2025 to ship the AI Driver in next-generation ProPILOT from fiscal 2027; on 11 March Wayve, Uber and Nissan agreed a Tokyo robotaxi pilot.
brief.the_case_p2: Wayve's brand now has to reach consumers, not only automakers: a robotaxi with its name on it goes on the road this year and a ProPILOT product carries it next. Formula E is the electric street-racing series in Wayve's home city, London, and in Tokyo, where the pilot launches; Nissan, the automaker most committed to Wayve, races a works team there. In Formula 1 Amazon's Zoox has already taken a seat with Williams.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The extension landed on 15 April and the Stellantis deal on 21 May; brand budgets reset in the quarter after a raise. The Tokyo E-Prix (25-26 July) and the London E-Prix season finale (15-16 August) both fall inside the window, and Season 13 rosters for the GEN4 car are set over the summer.
brief.why_team_para: Nissan is a Wayve shareholder, its first automaker to commit at scale, and its partner in the Tokyo robotaxi pilot; the works team is the natural stage to show that relationship to the public, and its roster carries no software, AI or autonomy partner, so the lane is open. Tokyo, the team's home E-Prix, comes as the pilot prepares to launch; the London finale sits a few miles from Wayve's headquarters. Andretti carries TWG AI; rival automakers' teams are closed.
brief.value_section_label: VALUE TO NISSAN FORMULA E TEAM
brief.value_content: MODE B - halo, with concrete mechanics. The AI Driver has no role in the race car, so the substance is demonstration, content and audience: a Wayve-driven Nissan LEAF running the ExCeL circuit in London and the Tokyo course on race weekend, a race-to-road content series on Nissan's e-4ORCE and Wayve's AI Driver, and hospitality for the automaker, regulator and city audiences both must win. In return: Official Embodied AI Partner status, livery presence.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Embodied AI Partner of the Nissan works team. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, spanning the Tokyo pilot and the fiscal-2027 ProPILOT launch. Estimated $2-4M a year, co-funded with Nissan's programme budget. Scope: autonomy-category exclusivity, demonstration laps at London and Tokyo, content, hospitality.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Kendall co-founded Wayve, has led it as CEO since 2020 and fronts every raise and automaker deal; a first sports partnership is his call, taken with Nissan. Path: Max Warburton, CFO since November 2024, formerly advisor to the Daimler and Mercedes-Benz board. No CMO listed.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Alex, Nissan races a works team in the two cities where Wayve's name goes public this year, Tokyo and London, and no autonomy brand sits on the Formula E grid. Zoox already races in Formula 1. 25 minutes before the Tokyo E-Prix?”

## The trigger, re-dated

The row's trigger was the 24 Feb 2026 Series D, 106 days before the row and therefore stale; the Wayve-Uber-Nissan Tokyo MoU of 11 Mar 2026 is 91 days before it, one day outside the window. The in-window trigger is **Wayve's own release of 15 Apr 2026: a $60M Series D extension from AMD, Arm and Qualcomm Ventures** (56 days before the row), reinforced by the **Stellantis STLA AutoDrive partnership of 21 May 2026**. Both are company-announced. The extension is small relative to the round, which is why timing is 14 and urgency 13, and why the brief leans on the Nissan relationship and the Tokyo pilot rather than on the capital.

## The team, confirmed

The row suggested Nissan Formula E; research confirms it as the honest choice for the reason the earlier signal check flagged: **Nissan is a Wayve shareholder and production partner**, so this is a warm, joint approach, not a cold pitch, and the brief says so (first risk, decision-maker bio, deal architecture). The Nissan Formula E Team's technical sponsor **Alpine Tech** (renewed for Season 12 per Nissan's newsroom) is not in the sponsor table and is therefore not written as "Brand at Team" in the copy. Post-row update: on 24 Jul 2026 Nissan announced it will also supply Andretti's GEN4 powertrain from Season 13; not public on the row date, so not in the brief.
